core_stats.cv_interpretation_warning: Celsius is an interval temperature scale with an arbitrary zero point (0°C = 273.15 K). Therefore, presenting CV = (s / mean_C) * 100% as a physically meaningful relative variability percentage is statistically invalid, as its numerical value changes arbitrarily under affine shifts. On the true ratio Kelvin scale, relative dispersion is 0.79% (s / mean_K, where mean_K = 303.39 K).

distribution_fit.diagnostics_summary: A model possessing the lowest AIC among candidates does NOT mean it provides a good absolute fit. Formal Kolmogorov-Smirnov goodness-of-fit testing rejects all candidate single distributions (p < 0.0001) due to strong annual seasonal cycles (cold winters vs. hot summers). The best candidate (lognorm) serves only as a relative parametric approximation; the empirical exceedance rate (0.95%) is the primary, directly verifiable baseline.

monte_carlo.note: Parametric random draws from fitted distribution. Validates numerical convergence of theoretical SF, not independent empirical model correctness.

simulation.recurrence_note: Inverse of long-run empirical exceedance rate (average historical spacing). Extreme heat clusters in multi-day events, so this does not represent a periodic schedule.

trend.practical_note: Daily slope statistically significant (p=< 0.0001 (approx 4.45e-77)) but total drift over the window is only +0.91 C - practically modest relative to annual variance. Complete calendar years (1950-2025) annual trend is +0.1128 C/decade (p=< 0.0001 (approx 5.46e-07)).

complete_years_trend.excluded_partial_year: 2026 (partial record through Oct 10, excluded from annual trend to prevent seasonal bias)
complete_years_trend.methodology: OLS regression on annual mean daily maximum temperatures across complete calendar years only
complete_years_trend.limitations_note: While complete-year annual aggregation removes intra-annual seasonality and daily autocorrelation, annual means may still exhibit low-frequency inter-annual climatic persistence (e.g., ENSO, decadal oscillations); OLS inference should be interpreted with caution.

transition_probabilities.limitations_note: Transition probabilities and clustering metrics reflect combined synoptic weather persistence and strong seasonal concentration (summer). They must not be interpreted as stationary, time-invariant physical constants across all calendar seasons.

dependence.interpretation: Extreme days exhibit pronounced serial persistence (lag-1 autocorrelation=0.9039, longest run=5 consecutive days, mean run=1.6 days). Crucially, P(Hot tomorrow | Hot today) = 38.6%, compared to only 0.6% if today is cool. Furthermore, 64.9% of all extreme days occur as part of multi-day heatwave episodes, demonstrating that extreme heat arrives in persistent waves rather than isolated events.

synthesis.formula_note: index_score (0-100) = [empirical_exceedance_rate * (1 + trend_adjustment) * (1 + clustering_adjustment)] * 100. This metric is an exploratory composite decision-support indicator, NOT a formal calibrated statistical probability.

dataset_info.underlying_model: ECMWF ERA5 Reanalysis (~0.25 deg grid resolution)
dataset_info.grid_point_disclosure: Data represents ECMWF ERA5 reanalysis grid point (19.0861°N, 72.8529°E, elevation 6.0m), not a single physical weather station sensor.
dataset_info.citation: Open-Meteo.com Historical Weather Archive API (ERA5 Reanalysis by ECMWF). Data retrieved for Mumbai, Maharashtra, India (Requested: 19.076° N, 72.8777° E; ERA5 Grid Point: 19.086115° N, 72.85291° E) spanning 1950-01-01 to 2026-10-10.
limitations: ECMWF ERA5 reanalysis data represents a ~0.25° (~25–31 km) grid cell; localized coastal microclimates and urban heat island effects are smoothed.
Archive updates lag real-time by approximately 2–5 days due to ERA5 assimilation cycles.
Daily maximum reflects 2-meter air temperature over the calendar day in Asia/Kolkata timezone.

validation_summary.verification_target_nature: ECMWF ERA5 Reanalysis Grid Proxy (Area-averaged cell). Notice: Reanalysis estimates share numerical parameterization errors with NWP models and do not constitute independent physical station verification.
validation_summary.validation_rule: Strict out-of-sample discipline: Only forecasts fetched prior to the target date's heating window can be validated once subsequent observations finalize. Same-day post-peak retrievals and unobserved future dates are strictly excluded from MAE and bias metrics.

open_meteo_nwp_grid.character: Inland / suburban Mumbai grid cell (~25 km resolution)

imd_santacruz_station.character: Suburban airport basin influenced by warm continental easterly land breeze before delayed afternoon sea breeze; closely aligns with NWP model grid temperatures.

imd_colaba_station.character: Coastal peninsula station buffered by marine sea breezes on three sides; typically 2–4°C cooler than suburban Santacruz and the inland grid cell during October heat.

meteorological_comparison.meteorological_explanation: ERA5 reanalysis and operational NWP models represent area-averaged atmospheric grid cells (~25 km) rather than point thermometer shelters. During post-monsoon 'October Heat' (following monsoon withdrawal), clear skies and easterly continental winds delay the cooling sea breeze, causing inland and suburban Mumbai (Santacruz basin and ERA5 grid) to spike to 36.8–37.6°C while coastal Colaba remains moderated. HeatSense presents the authentic raw NWP response without artificial modification.
